correctness.rationale: For n=mr,m,r≥2, cyclic block maps f_a(jr+u)=r(j+1 mod m)+(u+a_j mod r), Σa_j≡1 modr, are single n-cycles because f_a^m translates each block by one. The sign of f_a^t(x)−x for t not divisible by m is determined by block order; for t multiple m it is determined by internal rotation, so all r^(m−1) choices give one signature. Conversely for any n-cycle with that signature, g=f^m has exactly m r-cycles and exactly m descending points, at the block maxima. Every finite permutation cycle must have a descent, forcing g-orbits to equal the consecutive blocks, then monotonicity of all other entries forces their standard rotation. Commuting f and g makes f permute blocks, whose time-one sign inequalities force the successor block permutation; rotational equivariance then forces an internal translation on each block with sum shifts one. Thus no other cycles lie in that fiber. Independent complete n-cycle enumeration for n=4,6,8,9 verified exact fibers 2,3,4,8,4,9 across six factorizations; full proof holds for all m,r.
residual_risks: The exact count is for one explicit complete signature, not the maximal fiber across all signatures or global interval dynamics.
